evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:757-760 — PmApiClient::new() does `reqwest::Client::builder().timeout(..).build().expect("Failed to create HTTP client")`. reqwest::ClientBuilder::build() is fallible (TLS backend init, proxy-from-env parse); on failure this panics instead of returning a Result the composition root can log and fail-closed on.

Consistency smell strengthening the finding: the SAME AppState constructor that calls this (state.rs:948 `PmApiClient::new(config.pm_api_health_url.clone(), 5)`) builds a sibling reqwest client 3 lines later — the SSO oauth client at state.rs:956-960 — with the resilient `.build().unwrap_or_default()`. Two reqwest builders, same startup path, inconsistent failure handling: one degrades gracefully, the other panics. PmApiClient::new should mirror the sibling (unwrap_or_default) or return Result so the single caller at state.rs:948 can decide.

This is the exact pattern the team already accepted and fixed in sibling segments: done/accepted findings code-review-api-core-push-fanout-client-build-expect (push_fanout.rs built 3 reqwest clients with .expect() in production constructors) and code-review-api-core-api-call-client-build-expect (api_call.rs:308). state.rs:760 is the reality-server instance of the same precedent; same vector, same score=1.

Severity LOW, identical rationale to the accepted api-core precedents: PmApiClient::new() is reached only from AppState::new()/build at startup (state.rs:948), so the practical effect is a fail-fast crash at boot rather than a per-request panic — close to the acceptable startup-validation pattern.
